sources.title: 10, 12 AND 14, LOWTHER STREET
sources.author: Historic England / National Heritage List for England
sources.locator: Location L213–227; Details L228–240; listing and amendment dates L179–186
sources.quote_note: Non-contiguous location and Details labels; ellipses explicit.
sources.observed_relation: The entry places the specified Lowther Street buildings under Cumberland (Unitary Authority); its Details heading names CARLISLE and LOWTHER STREET. The narrative dates the vaults and extension to 1868 and 1881.
sources.limits: This is a positive street/city/authority binding, not a personal birthpoint; the buildings are not claimed to be Walker’s house.

sources.title: Landscape and Townscape Appraisal: St Cuthbert’s Garden Village
sources.author: LUC (Land Use Consultants Ltd), in association with Nick Haynes; commissioned by Carlisle City Council
sources.source_kind: original council-commissioned landscape and townscape appraisal
sources.locator: cover L0–6 and final version L26–31; §9.11 printed p58 / parsed L2211–2218; village wording §9.16 L2257–2260
sources.short_quote: Carleton is a hamlet and wider township in the historic Parish of St Cuthbert Without, two miles south-east of Carlisle
sources.observed_relation: The compound is positively bound: Carleton is a rural hamlet and township of historic St Cuthbert Without, two miles southeast of Carlisle, on the A6 London Road. The report also calls the settlement a village, so village/hamlet wording is not treated as a type contradiction.
sources.feature_type: hamlet; wider township; village in subsequent text
sources.limits: The quoted relation itself does not name a county. The county layer comes from the separately attributed historical gazetteer and catalogue. Not a new birth clause.

sources.title: Carleton, Carlisle
sources.author: Samuel Lewis, A Topographical Dictionary of England, 7th edition, London, 1848; extract reproduced by Newcastle University Co-Curate
sources.source_kind: explicitly attributed primary gazetteer transcription on university host
sources.locator: L7–8 for attributed Lewis extract; L10 for distinct alternative Carletons
sources.short_quote: CARLETON, a township, in the parish of St. Cuthbert, Carlisle, union of Carlisle, Cumberland ward, E. division of the county of Cumberland
sources.observed_relation: Lewis’s attributed entry gives Carleton as a township of St Cuthbert, Carlisle, in the eastern division of Cumberland, and specifies 2½ miles southeast of Carlisle. Host warns that Penrith and Copeland Carletons are distinct.
sources.feature_type: township (Lewis); modern host calls it village
sources.limits: Original 1848 page scan was not opened. The host’s modern description misspells the name Calerton; that misspelling is not adopted as a historical alias. Host modern overview is not a second witness independent of its extract.

sources.title: Old Cumbria Gazetteer – Carleton, St Cuthbert Without
sources.author: Old Cumbria Gazetteer compiler not identified in accessed text; original map makers are individually attributed
sources.source_kind: regional catalogue/transcriptions referencing OS County Series and named historical maps
sources.locator: header L5–10; OS reference L23–25; Ogilby L76–83; Bowen L107–114
sources.short_quote: Carleton, St Cuthbert Without … county:- Cumbria … locality type:- locality … locality type:- buildings
sources.observed_relation: Catalogue header locates this Carleton under St Cuthbert Without, formerly Cumberland, county Cumbria. It separately indexes OS County Series Cmd24.9, Ogilby 1675, Bowen 1720 and other named map editions.
